Fact.Name: Has cash or charge tips not reported to an employer
Fact.Description: Screener for #26 (TY2026, filed in 2027). Form 4137 (2025), page 1, "Who must file": "You must file Form 4137 if you received cash and charge tips of $20 or more in a calendar month and didn't report all of those tips to your employer." Pub. 531 (12-2024), page 5: "If you received $20 or more in cash and charge tips in a month from any one job and didn't report all of those tips to your employer, you must report the social security, Medicare, and Additional Medicare taxes on the unreported tips as additional tax on your return." 26 U.S.C. 3121(q): "tips received by an employee in the course of his employment shall be considered remuneration for such employment"; 3121(a)(12)(B) excludes "cash tips received by an employee in any calendar month ... unless the amount of such cash tips is $20 or more". 26 U.S.C. 3102(c)(1): employer withholding applies "only to such tips as are included in a written statement furnished to the employer pursuant to section 6053(a)"; 3102(c)(4): any excess "shall be paid by the employee." (statute text as rendered by LII) Placeholder false so returns that never see the screen are unaffected.

Fact.Name: Knockout: unreported tips (Form 4137 / Schedule 2 line 5)
Fact.Description: Form 4137 (social security and Medicare tax on unreported tips, Schedule 2 line 5) is not supported. Without this knockout, unreported tips would be silently left out of income and of the employee share of social security and Medicare tax. Cites: see /hasUnreportedTips. W-2 box 8 allocated tips are handled separately by formW2s /flowKnockoutAllocatedTips.
